from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "Classical objects exist in definite, singular states.",
            "Quantum systems allow for multiple states simultaneously.",
            "State vectors represent these quantum states mathematically."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("The Classical vs. Quantum World", lecture_lines)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        ball = Dot(color=WHITE, radius=0.3)
        self.place_at_grid(ball, 'B2', scale_factor=1.0)
        table = Line(start=LEFT*1.5, end=RIGHT*1.5, color=GREY).next_to(ball, DOWN)
        self.add(ball, table)
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#FFFFFF")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        wave = FunctionGraph(lambda x: 0.5 * np.sin(4 * x), x_range=[-1.5, 1.5], color="#00FF00")
        self.place_at_grid(wave, 'E2', scale_factor=0.8)
        self.add(wave)
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#00FF00")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        vector = Arrow(start=ORIGIN, end=UP*1.5 + RIGHT*0.5, color="#FFFF00")
        label = MathTex(r"\vec{\psi}", color="#FFFF00")
        self.place_at_grid(vector, 'C5', scale_factor=1.0)
        label.next_to(vector.get_end(), UP, buff=0.1)
        self.add(vector, label)
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#FFFF00")
        
        self.wait(2)

class Section2Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Defining Superposition", [
            "Superposition follows the linear combination principle.",
            "Alpha and beta scale the basic states.",
            "These act as complex probability amplitudes.",
            "Think of them as spinning circular phasors.",
            "Together they form a simultaneous quantum existence."
        ])
        
        # Elements
        psi = MathTex(r"|\psi\rangle").set_color("#0000FF")
        state0 = MathTex(r"|0\rangle").set_color("#FFFF00")
        state1 = MathTex(r"|1\rangle").set_color("#FF0000")
        lin_comb = MathTex(r"|\psi\rangle = \alpha|0\rangle + \beta|1\rangle").set_color(WHITE)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(FadeIn(psi), FadeIn(self.lecture[0]))
        self.place_at_grid(psi, "B2", scale_factor=2.0)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(GRAY), FadeIn(self.lecture[1]))
        self.place_at_grid(state0, "B4", scale_factor=1.5)
        self.place_at_grid(state1, "B6", scale_factor=1.5)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(GRAY), FadeIn(self.lecture[2]))
        self.place_in_area(lin_comb, "D1", "E6", scale_factor=1.2)
        self.play(Write(lin_comb))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(GRAY), FadeIn(self.lecture[3]))
        # Representation of phasors
        phasor_alpha = Circle(radius=0.5, color="#FFFF00").set_fill(opacity=0.3)
        phasor_beta = Circle(radius=0.5, color="#FF0000").set_fill(opacity=0.3)
        self.place_at_grid(phasor_alpha, "F2")
        self.place_at_grid(phasor_beta, "F5")
        self.play(Create(phasor_alpha), Create(phasor_beta))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[3].animate.set_color(GRAY), FadeIn(self.lecture[4]))
        self.play(FadeOut(psi), FadeOut(state0), FadeOut(state1))
        self.wait(2)

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "Measurement forces a collapse into single states.",
            "Born rule defines the probability of outcomes.",
            "Square the amplitudes to find the probability.",
            "Think of this as a shrinking cloud.",
            "The interaction picks one definite reality."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("The Measurement Problem & Collapse", lecture_lines)
        
        # Create objects
        cloud = Dot(radius=0.5, color="#FF00FF").set_opacity(0.6)
        measure_icon = Text("👁", font_size=48, color=WHITE)
        measure_label = Text("Measure", font_size=18, color=WHITE)
        measure_group = VGroup(measure_icon, measure_label).arrange(DOWN)
        
        # Initial placement
        self.place_in_area(cloud, "B2", "D4")
        self.place_at_grid(measure_group, "B5")
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(YELLOW)
        self.play(FadeIn(cloud), FadeIn(measure_group))
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color(YELLOW)
        self.wait(1)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[2].set_color(YELLOW)
        prob_formula = MathTex(r"P = |\alpha|^2", color=YELLOW)
        self.place_at_grid(prob_formula, "E2")
        self.play(Write(prob_formula))
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.lecture[3].set_color(YELLOW)
        # Animate cloud shrinking
        self.play(
            cloud.animate.scale(0.1).set_color("#00FFFF").set_opacity(1.0),
            FadeOut(prob_formula)
        )
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.lecture[4].set_color(YELLOW)
        self.play(
            measure_group.animate.set_color(RED),
            Indicate(cloud)
        )
        self.wait(2)

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "Bloch spheres map all possible qubit states.",
            "North pole represents our zero state.",
            "South pole represents our one state.",
            "The surface shows all possible superpositions.",
            "Rotation traces the path between states."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("Visualization: The Bloch Sphere", lecture_lines)
        
        # --- Animation Setup ---
        sphere = Sphere(radius=1.5, color=WHITE, fill_opacity=0.1)
        # Use place_in_area to position the sphere properly in the right grid
        self.place_in_area(sphere, 'A1', 'F6', scale_factor=1.0)
        
        vector = Arrow(start=ORIGIN, end=UP * 1.5, color="#00FF00", buff=0)
        vector.move_to(sphere.get_center())
        
        north_label = MathTex(r"|0\rangle").next_to(sphere.get_top(), UP, buff=0.1)
        south_label = MathTex(r"|1\rangle").next_to(sphere.get_bottom(), DOWN, buff=0.1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#00FFFF")
        self.play(Create(sphere), run_time=1.0)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#00FFFF")
        self.play(Create(vector), Write(north_label), run_time=1.0)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#00FFFF")
        self.play(Write(south_label), run_time=1.0)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.lecture[2].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[3].set_color("#00FFFF")
        self.play(sphere.animate.set_color("#FFFF00").set_fill(opacity=0.3), run_time=1.0)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.lecture[3].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[4].set_color("#00FFFF")
        # Rotating the vector
        self.play(Rotate(vector, angle=PI, about_point=sphere.get_center()), run_time=2.0)
        self.wait(1)

        lecture_lines = ["Superposition enables massive parallel processing power.", 
                         "Quantum algorithms explore all paths simultaneously.", 
                         "This shifts our logic beyond binary."]
        self.setup_layout("Summary & Real-World Impact", lecture_lines)

outline.topic: Superposition and Quantum States: The Architecture of Reality
outline.target_audience: Undergraduate science students or advanced high school students

sections.title: The Classical vs. Quantum World (0:00-0:45)
sections.content: Establish prerequisite knowledge: In classical physics, an object has a definite state (like a coin being Heads or Tails). Introduce the 'State Vector' concept as a mathematical arrow in a vector space.
sections.example: A spinning coin on a table: Before it stops, is it heads or tails? In our macroscopic world, we call it 'random'; in the quantum world, it is a specific state.

sections.title: Defining Superposition (0:45-2:00)
sections.content: Explain Superposition using the Linear Combination principle: |Ψ⟩ = α|0⟩ + β|1⟩. Use visual animation where α and β represent complex probability amplitudes, shown as circular vectors (phasors) on a complex plane.
sections.example: A musical note: A single pure tone (0 or 1) vs. a chord (superposition). The chord is not 'one or the other,' but a simultaneous existence of both frequencies.

sections.title: The Measurement Problem & Collapse (2:00-3:30)
sections.content: Illustrate the Born Rule: The probability of finding a state is |α|² or |β|². Use a visual 'gate' animation where the wavefunction collapses from a spread-out cloud into a single point upon interaction.
sections.example: Schrödinger’s Cat: A cat in a box with a device triggered by a radioactive decay. Until we peek inside (measure), the cat exists in a superposition of |Alive⟩ and |Dead⟩.

sections.title: Visualization: The Bloch Sphere (3:30-4:30)
sections.content: Introduce the Bloch Sphere as the standard geometric representation of a qubit. Show the poles as |0⟩ and |1⟩, and the surface as all possible superpositions.
sections.example: An arrow pointing to the North Pole is |0⟩. An arrow pointing to the Equator is an equal superposition (Hadamard state). As we rotate the arrow, we move between quantum states.

sections.title: Summary & Real-World Impact (4:30-5:00)
sections.content: Recap: Superposition allows quantum computers to process massive amounts of data simultaneously. End with a forward-looking thought on how these states move us beyond binary logic.
sections.example: Comparing a classical maze runner (trying one path at a time) to a quantum particle (exploring all paths of the maze simultaneously).
